open_rights_questions.subject: Remotion Company License eligibility
open_rights_questions.question: Does the organization deploying this skill fall inside the Remotion Free License eligibility (individual, non-profit, or for-profit organization with up to 3 employees, per the license text read from the installed remotion package), or must it hold a Company License from remotion.pro before production use?

open_rights_questions.subject: Redistribution of the Remotion compositor's bundled FFmpeg
open_rights_questions.question: The compositor's bundled FFmpeg binary reports a configuration combining GPL enablement with the libfdk-aac library. May that binary be redistributed (for example inside a client runtime bundle), and under what terms?
open_rights_questions.basis: the bundled binary's own -version output, run in this session; the compositor package ships no license statement
open_rights_questions.resolution: On the texts available, the bundled binary is not redistributable in its shipped configuration, and this release redistributes no copy of it. MG-048 re-ran the binary on the provisioned runtime: its configuration combines --enable-gpl with --enable-libfdk-aac, --enable-libx264, --enable-libx265, and --enable-libmp3lame. The FFmpeg project's own legal page states that when GPL-covered parts are used, the GPL applies to all of FFmpeg, and its checklist for a distributable build is to compile without --enable-gpl and without --enable-nonfree; libfdk-aac is the project's nonfree component, and the project treats the GPL-plus-nonfree combination as one that may not be redistributed. The compositor package ships no license statement that says otherwise (re-verified). Disposition for this release: the skill ships no FFmpeg code, the provisioner downloads the compositor package from npm at install time, and no runtime bundle containing this binary may be handed to anyone outside the deploying organization unless a build without the nonfree combination, or a vendor statement covering redistribution, exists. Neither exists on current texts.
open_rights_questions.resolution_basis: binary self-report re-run by MG-048; FFmpeg project legal page (ffmpeg.org/legal.html) read by MG-048; package contents re-listed by MG-048

open_rights_questions.subject: License coverage of @remotion/media and @remotion/compositor-* packages
open_rights_questions.question: These eight packages ship no license field and no license file. Are they covered by the Remotion License as the vendor intends, and may they be redistributed with the runtime?
open_rights_questions.basis: installed artifacts and both committed locks inspected in this session; no license statement found in any of the three sources
open_rights_questions.resolution: MG-048 re-verified the artifact fact: all eight packages still ship no license field and no license file. MG-048 also read the root of the vendor's monorepo (remotion-dev/remotion) at tag v4.0.535: it carries the Remotion License, whose grant speaks of 'the software' without enumerating packages, and the eight packages are version-locked parts of that same 4.0.535 release, published from that repository. What the build may therefore claim: use of these packages as part of Remotion 4.0.535 is governed by the Remotion License, including its eligibility tiers (ORQ-01, the deployer's own decision) and its prohibition on selling a derivative of Remotion itself. What remains unclaimed, because no text states it: an artifact-level redistribution permission for these packages standing alone. This release does not redistribute them (the provisioner downloads them from the npm registry at install time), so the release needs no such claim. Residual missing fact, recorded rather than papered over: a license statement inside the artifacts themselves.
open_rights_questions.resolution_basis: installed artifacts re-inspected by MG-048; vendor monorepo root LICENSE.md at tag v4.0.535 read by MG-048

open_rights_questions.subject: libvips LGPL duties at redistribution time
open_rights_questions.question: The @img/sharp-libvips packages state LGPL-3.0-or-later in metadata and ship no license text. If the provisioned runtime is redistributed, confirm the LGPL duties for libvips (library source availability and relinking posture) are met at that time.
open_rights_questions.basis: package metadata in the installed artifacts and the committed lock, read in this session
open_rights_questions.resolution: The duties are now stated from the text, and their trigger does not occur in this release. The LGPL-3.0 text (read from this host's /usr/share/common-licenses/LGPL-3) attaches its duties when the library is conveyed inside a combined work: the work must be accompanied by the LGPL and GPL texts; the library's corresponding source must be provided or offered (written offer or network source location); the library portion stays licensed under the LGPL; and the recipient must remain able to modify the library and use the modified library with the combined work, a posture the shipped form supports because libvips ships as separate shared-object files loaded by sharp at runtime rather than being linked into a single binary. The libvips packages state the license in metadata only and ship no text; that documentation gap is recorded on their records. Disposition for this release: no duty is triggered, because the release redistributes no runtime; the provisioner downloads sharp and libvips from npm at install time. Whoever first bundles the provisioned runtime for redistribution must execute the source-availability duty for the exact libvips build at that time; this register claims no such satisfaction in advance.
open_rights_questions.resolution_basis: LGPL-3.0 text read from /usr/share/common-licenses/LGPL-3 by MG-048; package records re-inspected by MG-048

records.name: Liberation Sans

license_source.detail: /usr/share/doc/fonts-liberation/copyright read in this session (License: SIL-OFL-1.1; Reserved Font Name Liberation). Font binaries referenced by the runtime at /usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf and LiberationSans-Bold.ttf; the shared design fixture alias font-fixture-sans resolves to this family on this host.

records.notice_requirements: The OFL requires the copyright notice and the license to accompany the font software when the font itself is redistributed, and modified versions must not use the Reserved Font Name.
records.deployment_notes: The runtime measures and renders text with this font locally; glyphs rendered into video frames are output, not a redistribution of the font software. Shipping the TTF files themselves (for example inside a client bundle) would trigger the OFL conditions above.

records.name: KIE.ai (generated imagery route)

license_source.detail: KIE.ai Terms of Use at https://kie.ai/terms-of-use read in full in this session (operators named there: NEXUSAI SERVICES LLC and INNOLEAP AI LLC). The terms address user-uploaded content ownership and the license the user grants the operator to run the service; they contain no clause that grants or defines rights in AI-generated outputs.

records.deployment_notes: Rights in images generated through KIE.ai are therefore not established by KIE's own Terms of Use as read; they depend on the underlying model providers' terms, which were not reviewed in this session. Do not treat a generated asset as cleared for commercial use on the basis of the KIE terms alone, ORQ-05. Generated assets enter jobs through the MG-011 intake like any other asset (recorded path, hash, provenance with source generated_kie).
